name: Monport GT 100W Fiber
tagline: 100W Split fiber laser engraver with autofocus from Monport
tldr: Monport GT 100W Fiber is the 100W SKU on the Monport monport gt line. Monport GT 30W brings split-cabinet fiber marking with autofocus: useful for varying part heights. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.
mainObjective: Maximum fiber marking speed and depth in the line

priceRange.note: Official Monport store, Oct 2026: $6,600 to $7,050 depending on bundle

engraveExample.description: Filled logo on stainless steel plate

pros: Highest listed marking depth in the GT line below the 200W: 0.15 mm
MOPA source (2–500 ns, 1–3,000 kHz) with colour marking, so one machine covers colour and depth
Fastest GT in our stainless benchmark: about 2–5 minutes for a filled 10 × 10 cm logo
cons: About $1,900–2,100 more than the GT 60W MOPA for depth and speed, not new capabilities
The laser source is covered for 1 year, against 2 years for the rest of the machine
More power means more fumes and spatter on deep jobs: extraction and an enclosure become essential

faq.question: How much deeper does the GT 100W engrave than the 60W?
faq.answer: Monport lists a maximum marking depth of 0.15 mm for the GT 100W, against 0.10 mm for the GT 50W and 60W. Pulse energy is the same 1.5 mJ as the 60W, so the gain comes from average power: more material removed per second on deep engraving and cut-outs. In our benchmark, a filled 10 × 10 cm logo on stainless takes about 2–5 minutes.

faq.question: Can the GT 100W cut sheet metal?
faq.answer: Thin sheet, in multiple passes. Monport's claim for the GT series is cutting thin metals under 3 mm, and the 100W has the most headroom for it short of the 200W. For regular cutting of 1–3 mm steel, a dedicated fiber cutting machine with assist gas is faster and leaves cleaner edges.

faq.question: Is the GT 100W worth it over the GT 60W MOPA?
faq.answer: It costs $6,600 (pre-order) to $6,800 (in stock) on Monport's store in October 2026, roughly $1,900–2,100 more than the 60W. Colour range, pulse settings and the 175 × 175 mm field are the same. The extra money buys depth and speed for production: deep logos on tools, embossing, coins and cut-outs. For colour and surface marking alone, the 60W is enough.

standoutFeatures.title: Depth for production engraving
standoutFeatures.body: 0.15 mm listed maximum marking depth, 50% more than the GT 50W and 60W, with a 10,000 mm/s top speed. Suited to deep tool marking, embossing and coin work.

standoutFeatures.title: MOPA control at high power
standoutFeatures.body: The 100W keeps the 2–500 ns pulse range of the 60W, so the same machine handles colour marking, delicate plastics and deep engraving without a second laser.

beginnerNotes: This profile is the 100W SKU on Monport GT Fiber. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Push speed only after depth tests on your metal alloy. Cooling and lens cleanliness matter more at this power level.
primaryUse: High-power fiber for metal-focused shops needing line-top throughput

editorialDepth.advantages: Monport GT Fiber 100W fits shops that mark stainless, aluminum, and tools daily without a CO₂ bay. A solid bench option for jewelry, tags, and small batches.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if wood, leather, or cast acrylic pay your bills. Deep metal cutting and large industrial panels often need more fiber headroom or a different machine class.
